name: 9x19mm
summary: Caliber - base damage 22, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 1.

beginner.whatItIs: The pistol and submachine gun round, and the cheapest ammunition on the list at a dollar a shot.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its Flesh variant opens at a lower level than any other calibre's, so it is usually the first ammunition upgrade a new player is even allowed to buy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Feed it to a sidearm or an SMG for close-range work. It costs so little to run that it is the sensible round to learn the maps with.

name: 5.56x45mm
summary: Caliber - base damage 28, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 1.5.

beginner.whatItIs: The rifle calibre shared by more weapons than any other in the game, including the free starting rifle.
beginner.whyItMatters: Standardising on one calibre means a single stock of ammunition serves several of your guns, so you spend less money holding two supplies you only half use.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Build around it early. It is the cheapest way to keep more than one weapon fed while your bank is still small.

name: 7.62x39mm
summary: Caliber - base damage 42, types FMJ / HP / AP.

beginner.whatItIs: A heavier rifle round that trades shots per second for damage per shot, currently carried by the SKS.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its Piercing variant unlocks earlier than any other calibre's, so this is the first place in the game where you can buy a real answer to armour.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it when you would rather land fewer, harder hits than more, lighter ones. Keep levelling it if you want armour penetration before the rest of the lobby has it.

name: 5.45x39mm
summary: Caliber - base damage 26, types FMJ / HP / AP.

beginner.whatItIs: The AK74's rifle round: a small, fast bullet with modest damage behind it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It sits close to the common rifle calibre on damage but only one weapon draws from it, so stocking it is a commitment to that single gun.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when the AK74 is genuinely the rifle you want to run. If you swap rifles often, a calibre with more weapons behind it wastes less of your money.

beginner.whatItIs: A revolver round used by the Judge, sold in boxes rather than as single rounds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its damage figure has not been published yet, so it is one of the few calibres you cannot compare against the others on paper before you commit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when you are set on the Judge. Treat its damage as unknown rather than assuming it matches the other large pistol rounds.

name: 7.62x54mmR
summary: Caliber - base damage 55, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 6.

beginner.whatItIs: The long-range rifle and machine gun round, shared by the PKM, the SVD and the Mosin Nagant.
beginner.whyItMatters: It hits hard for how early you can reach it, and three very different weapons all draw on the same stock, which keeps a reach-focused loadout on one supply.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it when your kit is built around distance, whether that is a marksman rifle or a machine gun holding an angle. It costs several times what a pistol round does, so do not hose it downrange.

name: .45 ACP
summary: Caliber - base damage 30, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 1.

beginner.whatItIs: A heavier pistol round behind the M1911 and the Super-45, priced the same as the cheapest pistol ammunition.
beginner.whyItMatters: You get more damage per shot than the small pistol round for identical money, but you wait far longer before either of its upgrades unlocks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it over the cheaper pistol round when you want a sidearm that ends a close fight in fewer hits and you are not counting on ammunition upgrades to get there.

name: .308 Win
summary: Caliber - base damage 60, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 4.

beginner.whatItIs: A full-power rifle round with the highest published damage per shot of any calibre here, used by the FAL, the BMR-308 and the MK22.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is expensive per shot and its armour-piercing variant is gated further out than anything else in the game, which makes it a calibre you grow into rather than start on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when one well-placed shot matters more than volume of fire, and when you can afford to miss a few and still buy the next loadout.

name: .50AE
summary: Caliber - base damage 49, types FMJ / HP / AP, standard round $ 4.

beginner.whatItIs: The Deagle's oversized pistol round, priced like rifle ammunition rather than pistol ammunition.
beginner.whyItMatters: It puts rifle-weight damage into a sidearm slot, and you pay for that twice: at the counter, and in the very high level its upgrades sit behind.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Carry it when the sidearm is meant to win fights on its own, not just cover a reload.

name: 12 Gauge
summary: Caliber - types FMJ / HP / AP / Rifled Slug.

beginner.whatItIs: The shotgun round for the MP43 and the M500, and the only calibre with a fourth ammunition type on top of the usual three.
beginner.whyItMatters: That fourth type, the rifled slug, turns a spreading weapon into a single-projectile one, which is a bigger change than any other calibre can offer you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it for indoor and doorway fighting. The slug opens at WARDOG level 41 and is worth taking if you want the same shotgun to stay useful past close range.

beginner.whatItIs: The anti-materiel round behind the AMR 50, and by a wide margin the most expensive ammunition in the game. Only the standard type is documented for it so far.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single round is $50, more than any pistol box on the vendor screen ($10 to $33).
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only with a plan behind it: a prepared position, a target worth the price, and a way out afterwards. It is not a round to carry casually.

beginner.whatItIs: A calibre the game has confirmed exists, with no ammunition types, unlock levels, prices or damage published for it yet.
beginner.whyItMatters: No weapon on the current list is recorded as feeding on it, so it points at content still to come rather than anything you can plan a loadout around.
beginner.whenToUseIt: There is nothing to decide here yet. Check it again after Early Access, when the missing figures should be filled in.

beginner.whatItIs: A heavy calibre listed as confirmed but otherwise undocumented: no types, no unlock levels, no prices, no damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Nothing in the current weapon list is recorded as firing it, which most likely means its weapon has not shipped yet.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Not a choice available to you today. Worth a second look at Early Access to see which weapon turns up alongside it.

beginner.whatItIs: A rifle calibre confirmed by name only, with none of its figures published.
beginner.whyItMatters: Like the other undocumented calibres, it has no weapon attached to it in the current list, so there is nothing to cost out or compare.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Skip it for now and re-check once the game is out and its numbers exist.
